title: Finding the bottleneck: application, database, network or infrastructure

videos.script: Lesson 8 told you how slow the box office is. This lesson finds out why. {{report}} A request passes through four layers. The client, the network, the application, the database. And under all of them, the machine itself. {{layers}} Any one of them can be the one that is full. Speed up anything else, and nobody notices. {{full}} So you read clocks. The client's clock, and the server's own, in a header it sends with every answer. Subtract one from the other, and you know which layer to open. {{clocks}} Then you ask three questions of each resource inside it. How busy is it? How much is waiting for it? Is it refusing anything? {{use}} The box office answers with four findings. A query that reads every row of a table. {{scan}} A lock held while a customer pays, so bookings go through one at a time. {{lock}} Forty milliseconds that are in no part of the code at all. {{tcp}} And a queue at the door that turns connections away. {{queue}} By the end you will have fixed all four, and checked that two people still cannot buy the same seat. {{race}}
